messages:
sam: hey team, spotted an odd billing surge on a hosted customer this morning — looks tied to streaming + reconnects + toolcalls. token graph in console jumps during reconnect windows :grimace:

maria: ugh. which route/region? any repro?

sam: us-west route. repro tiny: open a streaming session, trigger a toolcall mid-stream, force a client reconnect (TCP kill) and resume. billing shows provisional charge for the initial prefix, then again after resume.

sam: quick log snippet from router:
```
2026-03-20T09:12:01Z INFO session=abc123 route=us-west step=stream-prefix-captured tokens=42 provisional=true
2026-03-20T09:12:02Z INFO session=abc123 client=conn-19 disconnect reason=network
2026-03-20T09:12:04Z INFO session=abc123 reconnect resume=true route=us-west tokens=42 confirm_ack=false
2026-03-20T09:12:05Z INFO session=abc123 toolcall id=tc-7 truncated=true tokens=10 charged=true
2026-03-20T09:12:06Z INFO session=abc123 confirm_ack=true tokens_confirmed=52 charged=true
```

ted: hm so we charged provisional then charged again when confirmed? Do we mark provisional as reconciled and subtract if duplicated?

sam: seems we never reconcile provisional for streams that had a toolcall split across the reconnect. the toolcall traces create a new token charge path, router attributes to the new session id.

ops-telemetry: attaching the synthetic trace we pulled — sampling shows 0.3% of streaming sessions hit this pattern, but they’re high-token.

liz: for product thinking — customers see two charges back-to-back. Can console show provisional vs final and the session lineage?

maria: two quick hypotheses:
- attribution key uses session id + prefix id; reconnect creates new session id -> duplicate attribution
- toolcall truncation sets a charged=true flag early in the pipeline before we dedupe on confirm_ack

sam: yeah, plus our quota UI counts provisional against quota instantly (to honor SLOs) but billing ledger expects confirmed tokens on finalize. mismatch window.

ted: proposal: change router to tag provisional ledger entries with lineage_id (original_session|prefix_hash) and make finalization perform an idempotent upsert instead of raw insert. if upsert sees existing provisional, convert rather than append.

maria: implementation caveat — upsert at our scale can cause contention on the ledger write path. we already see hot keys for large sessions.

sam: alternative: grace-window approach — mark provisional entries with a 5s tentative TTL and only promote to confirmed on ack; if duplicate arrives within window, merge. That avoids synchronous upsert hot path.

ted: how does that interact with toolcalls that are truncated and charged mid-stream? e.g., we currently set charged=true immediately to avoid underbilling if client never reconnects.

sam: edge: if we delay promotion, short-lived disconnects might leave the customer underbilled if client abandons before confirm. but we can keep a provisional charge counter that decrements if duplicate confirmation happens, or convert provisional->confirmed atomically at promotion time. the key is to avoid double-insert.

ops-telemetry: current telemetry lacks a clear metric: "provisional_to_confirmed_merge_rate" and we don't expose session lineage in console. we can add a tag to traces: lineage_id and charge_state (provisional/confirmed/dropped).

liz: product asks for two UX pieces: (1) console toggle to show provisional vs final charges in a request timeline; (2) a note on invoices when provisional conversions happened during the billing period.

ted: billing side: invoices are generated from confirmed ledger only. if provisional got double-counted and later fixed we need reconciliation runs. do we have automated reconciliation for this pattern?

sam: we have nightly reconciliation that looks for later `reverse` events, but it's coarse-grained and we saw customer complaints before the nightly job ran.

maria: short-term fix idea: emit an alert whenever a session has >1 provisional insert for same lineage within 10s. ops can chase and trigger manual adjustment. medium-term: implement TTL-based merge and add lineage-aware promotion to confirmed.

ted: need to be careful with quotas — if console uses provisional for quota enforcement, customers could be blocked even if final billing would net to zero (after dedupe). we should decouple quota enforcement from provisional billing: use a soft quota for provisional and hard quota on confirmed.

sam: agree. propose:
- quota pipeline: provisional increments soft counter, not enforced; if soft > threshold send warning. confirmed increments hard counter that enforces blocking.
- billing pipeline: write provisional with lineage_id + TTL; on confirm, merge and promote, updating invoiceable tokens atomically.

ops-telemetry: will add metrics and a dashboard tile for "provisional vs confirmed discrepancy" and a heatmap by route/model.

liz: timeline? customers complaining now. we should do a fast patch (alert + docs + invoice note) and then a 2-week sprint for TTL merge + quota decoupling.

sam: I'll open an RFC for the TTL-merge design and a follow-up PR for console wiring (lineage display).

ted: ok, I'll add billing checks to the RFC for invariants we need (no double invoice, idempotent promotion).

maria: ops will add an on-call runbook and the alert rule.

billing-bot: invoice-service: created ticket #BILL-4523 for manual reconciliation on the affected customer.

sam: thanks all — tagging @liz to keep product updates flowing. will DM an initial repro script for QA. :thumbsup:
